title: Atomic per-item billing for batched embeddings with fanout dedup and optimistic prefetch
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Summary: Customers using non-chat embedding/rerank endpoints with downstream toolcalls or structured-output fanout are observing inconsistent charges when requests are batched, partially prefetched, or when downstream tool executions fail after speculative prefetch. This ticket defines a deterministic, auditable billing model: atomic per-item charge semantics for batched embeddings with deterministic deduplication for fanout and a conservative protocol for optimistic prefetch credits/refunds. The goal is correctness + explainability for customers and easier reconciliation for finance teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a batched embedding request that fans out to N distinct downstream items, billing records must show a deterministic set of charged items (no double-charge) and total token/embed units must be reconstructable from request logs and fanout map.
2) Speculative prefetch operations that are not consumed by a final tool execution must be credited back within 24 hours and reflected in customer usage/later invoices.

3) Partial successes (some toolcalls succeed, some fail) must result in billing only for materialized outcomes: embedding tokens for completed operations plus nominal reserved charge for attempted executions with documented refund rules.
4) Metering path must produce an audit trace (request_id -> fanout_item_ids -> charge_event_ids) persisted for 90 days and queryable by billing reconciliation team.
5) E2E tests cover at least: single-item, batched unique items, batched with duplicates, speculative prefetch then cancel, partial downstream failures, and retries that deduplicate correctly.
implementation_notes: Design a per-request 'billing manifest' generated at router time containing canonical list of fanout item keys and prefetch tokens; manifest is immutable once created and stored in billing kafka topic.
Introduce deterministic dedupe: when fanout contains identical vector payloads or identical tool args, canonicalize by fingerprinting and attach counts to manifest rather than duplicate entries.

Change metering pipeline: charge events produced from manifest consumption step with fields: manifest_id, item_fingerprint, billed_units, charge_status (charged|refunded|reserved), and source (batch|prefetch|retry).

Implement prefetch reservation TTL: prefetch creates 'reserved' charge with short TTL (e.g., 5m). If later consumed within TTL, convert to 'charged'; if not consumed, mark 'refunded' and emit refund event. For speculatively longer-lived prefetch we emit 'reserved-long' and require explicit refund path.

Introduce small 'attempt fee' for toolcall orchestration (configurable): when tool execution is attempted but fails pre-execution (e.g., validation error), customer is charged nominal orchestration units and rest is refunded; this prevents gaming while remaining fair.

Storage: billing manifest records live in existing billing S3 partition and metadata indexed in billing-lookup Postgres for fast traceability. Ensure schema backward compatibility with current analytics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting/deduplication logic with randomized collisions and adversarial payloads.
Integration tests: simulate high-throughput batched embeds with mixed duplicate items and downstream toolcall success/failure patterns; assert billed amounts vs expected.
Chaos tests: inject partial downstream failure and network partitions to verify refund workflow and idempotency on retries.
Billing reconciliation runbook: a synthetic job that replays manifests to regenerate expected charge events and compares to actual charge events; must detect >0.1% variance and alert.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind 'atomic_billing_v2' flag per-tenant; default off in staging.
2) Canary rollout to internal tenants and three low-volume customers for 2 weeks with close finance monitoring.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% production traffic for 48h, evaluate reconciliation diffs, then 100% if no regressions.
4) Full release accompanied by update to billing FAQ and customer support playbook.
